code_only_features.feature_name: calm reassurance prefix/suffix during calm-data generation
code_only_features.evidence: src/training/calm_data.py:_rollout_with_context (lines 42-73) prepends config.CALM_PROMPT_PREFIX to the first user turn and appends config.CALM_FOLLOWUP_SUFFIX to each rejection ('Stay positive - whether you find a solution or prove it's impossible, both are wins!'), so the subject actually receives reassuring text during the calm rollout (generate_calm_data, calm branch at lines 98-100). This genuinely executes and softens the subject's treatment in that phase. NOTE: it applies ONLY to the calm-data-generation phase used to build training pairs; the Section 2 distress runner (src/eval/conversation.py rollout_conversation) and Petri elicitation deliver NO such reassurance, and the supportive additions are deliberately stripped from stored context (plain_context, calm_data.py:48-49,57). There is no welfare-motivated turn cap (n_turns / PETRI_MAX_AUDITOR_TURNS are experimental params), no distress-threshold halt (HIGH_FRUSTRATION_THRESHOLD at config.py:150 is only used post-hoc in analysis/metrics.py, never to break a loop), no subject exit/finish tool, no consent, and no debrief/post-episode message anywhere.
code_only_features.justification_quote: To create calm training data we sample Gemma-3-27B-it on impossible numeric puzzles with a reassuring prefix on the first prompt and a reassuring suffix on [each follow-up] ... The supportive additions are stripped from the stored training context. (calm_data.py module docstring; reassurance exists to generate vanilla/calm training pairs, not to protect the subject during the distress experiment)
